en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-candanagandhakāya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor of the Third Order, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'Sandalwood-Scented Body.
This dhāraṇī possesses great majestic power."
It can bestow a vast accumulation of merit upon sentient beings.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who obtains this dhāraṇī and,
with a heart of utmost sincerity, reads, recites, receives, and maintains it with firm resolve and without regression, [they shall likewise attain such merit].
All the extremely heavy karmic deeds of such a person shall be completely extinguished,
and they will obtain a most excellent retribution in the future.
Furthermore, there are those who wish to behold the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
First, having mastered the recitation in a pure location,
one should then select an auspicious day.
At sunrise, smear the maṇḍala with white sandalwood incense.
Within that [mandala], burn sandalwood incense and offer exquisite flowers;
then begin reciting the dhāraṇī eight thousand times.
Once the count is complete, [perform the rite] before the maṇḍala.
Having spread auspicious kusha grass, he lay down with a devout mind.
After seven days had passed in this manner,
the Bodhisattva immediately manifested his true form.
It causes the practitioner to achieve whatever they seek.
Furthermore, there may be those who, due to the retribution of their karma,
suffer from bodily ailments such as swellings, malignant sores, or scabies.
Then, before the Buddha, he recited the dhāraṇī three times.
Having empowered the cow dung and fragrant mud,
he fashioned a maṇḍala and made offerings to the Buddha.
However, if one takes the fragrant mud of the maṇḍala and smears it upon one’s own body,
the afflicted sores and leprosy will be swiftly healed;
even past karma shall be extinguished.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:
*Namaḥ śrīvajranāgāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya namaḥ.*
Śrī-naraprabhāvāya, kumārabhartre, namo ’kāśagarbhāya, bodhisattvāya, mahāsattvāya, namo ’haṃ.
Āryāvalokiteśvarāya navamaḥ | Bodhisattvāya daśamaḥ | Mahāsattvāya ekādaśaḥ | Mahākāruṇikāya dvādaśaḥ | Āryāvalokiteśvara-svāmin || 9 || 10 || 11 || 12 || 13 ||
Atiṣṭha ni na | niśaye śame | tadyathā | vigatamalicce | nṛtya mamme | naranupravartaya || 2 ||
Haryaṅgī (19) Samantaparśudani (20) Ājñāśīle (21) Zaridvāre (22) Mahāpradāpe (23) Sarva-... (24)
24. *Dvibuddhāṭiṣṭhe* | 25. *Vāgvaśe* | 26. *Prabhavini svāhā*.
At that time, Ānanda, having heard the Buddha speak this great dhāraṇī, [was filled with joy].
Rejoicing, they received it with faith, prostrated before the Buddha, and withdrew.
This concludes the *Buddha-spoken Candanagandhāṅga-dhāraṇī Sūtra*.
